title: Adoption Journey Map — 90‑Day Lite Template
body:
Purpose:
This lightweight 90‑day adoption map is a modular template for Customer Success Managers to accelerate first value, track early health signals, and create repeatable handoffs that surface renewal opportunities. It is intentionally concise — meant to be adapted per account while preserving consistent measurement across customers.

How to use this template:
- Pick the relevant ‘use case lane’ (API integration, internal tooling, knowledge base ingestion) and prune tasks that aren’t applicable.
- Run the plan in sprints (weekly check-ins) rather than calendar days if the customer prefers operational cadence.
- Treat each 30‑day block as a hypothesis to validate; record outcomes in the Postmortem/Playbook section.

Outcome goals (examples — adapt for customer):
- Day 30: Customer has a repeatable example request flow, 1 internal champion running an integration test, and the first production call in a staging environment.
- Day 60: Integration is stable with automated end‑to‑end tests, internal docs created, and 2 internal users actively using features.
- Day 90: Customer has migrated a pilot workload, cost/latency targets are documented, and an internal business case is drafted for expansion.

Success metrics (pick 3 primary + 2 signals):
- Primary: "time_to_first_successful_call" <= 14 days, "active_users_30d" >= 2, "pilot_latency_p95" <= target
- Signals: "support_ticket_count_weekly" decreasing, "feature_flag_usage" increasing

Risk taxonomy (quick scan):
- Integration blockers: Customer network policies, missing auth keys, unsupported model variant. Mitigation: Dedicated troubleshooting session + network diagram walkthrough.
- Adoption blockers: No internal champion, unclear ownership. Mitigation: Identify escalation path; secure exec sponsor commit.
- Economics blockers: Unit cost exceeds expectation. Mitigation: Run Redwood Optimize suggestions and document expected savings after quantization/batching.

30/60/90 breakdown (actionable checklist):
- Days 0–30 (Discovery & First Value):
  - Kickoff: Align on success metrics, stakeholders, timeline (agenda below).
  - Inventory: Get API keys, network topology, compliance checklist, and sample dataset.
  - Quickstart: Run sample request with the customer, verify response parity, capture latency baseline.
  - Training: Short demo (30m) for engineers + product owner focused on integration patterns.
  - Deliverable: "First Call" checklist signed, shared snippet in customer repo or snippet file.

- Days 31–60 (Stabilize & Expand):
  - Hardening: Add retries/backoff, KV cache recommendations, and simple monitoring alerts.
  - Internal adoption: Walkthrough for two teammates, collect feedback on prompt templates and output drift.
  - Performance tuning: Try batching settings from Redwood Optimize and compare token cost per 1k requests.
  - Renewables: Capture early value metrics to start renewal timeline conversations.
  - Deliverable: Runbook doc with troubleshooting steps + sample alerts.

- Days 61–90 (Pilot to Production):
  - Pilot migration support: Assist with production toggles, traffic shaping, and canary rollout plan.
  - Eval and regression checks: Run small evals to ensure output quality remains stable after optimizations.
  - ROI capture: Co-author a short business case with usage projections and cost per query.
  - Renewal trigger prep: Identify renewal signal thresholds (usage, seat count, business impact) and recommended next steps.
  - Deliverable: "Pilot retrospective" + expansion recommendation and next engagement plan.

Weekly cadence & meeting templates:
- Weekly 30‑minute standup (owner: CSM)
  - 5m: Wins from the customer
  - 10m: Blockers and action items (technical or org)
  - 10m: Metrics review (calls, latency, errors, cost)
  - 5m: Next steps and owners

- Technical troubleshooting (ad hoc, 60m)
  - Goal: Reproduce issue, swap logs, confirm root cause, set action owners

- Executive sync (every 30 days, 20–30m)
  - Goal: Surface business impact and secure exec-level commitment for pilot/expansion

Sample customer emails (editable):
- Kickoff invite subject: "Kickoff — Redwood onboarding for <CUSTOMER-NAME> — Week of <DATE>"
  Hi <NAME>,

  Looking forward to our kickoff. Proposed agenda: 1) Introductions + success criteria, 2) Integration touchpoints and deliverables, 3) Timeline and risks. Please share any additional stakeholders.

  Thanks,
  <CSM NAME>

- Post‑30 summary subject: "30‑day check: first call, baseline metrics and next steps"
  Hi <NAME>,

  Congrats on getting the first call live. Key metrics: latency p95 = X ms, failed calls = Y, sample prompt results attached. Recommended next steps: 1) Add retry logic, 2) Schedule tuning session, 3) Share runbook with team.

  Cheers,
  <CSM NAME>

Decision log & hypotheses (short table to maintain):
- Hypothesis A: If we enable prefix caching, latency will drop by 20% for repeated prompts. Outcome: [pass/fail] — Notes.
- Hypothesis B: If we switch to 4-bit quantized weights, cost per token drops by ~30% with negligible quality regression for this workload. Outcome: [pass/fail] — Notes.

Renewal / expansion signals (operational):
- Strong signals: sustained weekly growth in production calls, 3+ internal users, explicit budget approval email request.
- Weak signals: intermittent calls, single engineer using the system, no internal documentation.

Quick Handoff checklist for next CSM or AE:
- Share runbook + login creds + integration artifacts
- Attach pilot retrospective and business case draft
- Highlight top 3 recommended improvements and estimated impact
- Note any unresolved risks or exec asks

Templates & artifacts to attach to customer folder:
- First Call Checklist (checkbox list)
- Runbook (troubleshooting + escalation contacts)
- Mini ROI one‑pager (numbers only)
- Eval prompt set and baseline outputs

Postmortem & learning capture (end of 90 days):
- What worked? What did not?
- Which hypotheses were validated? Which need follow up?
- Suggested changes to this template for similar customers (one paragraph)

Notes on customization: keep the template lean for SMBs (single page checklist) and expand to operational runbooks for enterprise customers with SRE integration. For privacy‑sensitive customers, swap any data examples with synthetic inputs and confirm KMS/HSM alignment in the first week.

Appendix — Short checklist snapshot (copy into Jira/Notion):
- [ ] Kickoff scheduled + success metrics agreed
- [ ] First call executed and latency baseline captured
- [ ] Runbook created and shared
- [ ] Two internal users trained
- [ ] Pilot migration plan documented
- [ ] Business case drafted
- [ ] Renewal/expansion recommendation sent

Contributors: Evelyn Park (author), Mateo Ruiz (technical reviewer), Priya Sinha (GTM commentary).

Version history: 0.1 draft — lightweight format for field teams; 0.2 planned — add performance tuning checklist and template Jira tasks.
